create.title: Popov 2024 truncated Voronoi formula source audit
create.statement_tex: Popov Theorem 5 states P(x)=-(x^(1/4)/pi) sum_(n<=N) r_2(n)n^(-3/4) cos(2pi sqrt(nx)+pi/4)+Delta_N P(x), with Delta_N P(x)<<sqrt(x/N) rbar(x)+rbar(N)log N and rbar(t)=t^(o(1)). At N asymp X^(1/2), the error is O_epsilon(X^(1/4+epsilon)). Theorem 4 and the J_1 asymptotic confirm the same radial constant and phase.
create.next_action: Use only for the exact Hardy--Voronoi normalization and target-sized truncation error; it supplies no new radial-sum estimate.

create.title: Exact global angular recombination of active M1
create.statement_tex: For the accepted exact dyadic denominator partition, actual Vaaler heights H_j=floor(D_j X^(-1/4)), and endpoint-star convention, the total active M1 stationary contribution equals -(4/pi)X^(1/4) Re{e(1/8) sum_(n<=16sqrt X) C_X^*(n)n^(-3/4)e(sqrt(Xn))}+O_W(log^2 X), where C_X^*(n)=sum_(h|n,q=n/h odd) chi_4(q) Omega_X^*(n,h) and Omega_X^*(n,h)=sum_j 1_(h<=H_j) Phi(h/(H_j+1))[w_j(2h sqrt(X/n))]^*. The inactive bottom range is separately O(X^(1/4)). The L-partition disappears exactly, while the D-partition leaves a floor-perturbed angular divisor symbol.
create.next_action: Separate the exact angular symbol by Mellin or Dirichlet-series methods without discarding height floors, the hard cone, or the endpoint star.

create.title: Global angular radial estimate for the active M1 aggregate
create.statement_tex: For the exact C_X^*(n) of M9-M1-global-angular-recombination, prove Re{e(1/8) sum_(n<=16sqrt X) C_X^*(n)n^(-3/4)e(sqrt(Xn))} <<_epsilon X^epsilon. This is sufficient for the total active M1 contribution and is strictly weaker than uniform blockwise M9-M1, but it does not imply an individual dyadic block estimate and is equivalent to the original global active M1 sum up to controlled transform and inactive-tail errors.
create.next_action: Derive a two-variable Mellin expansion of Omega_X^*(n,h), identify the resulting twisted divisor coefficients, and audit whether any mode admits cancellation beyond the accepted RCS bounds.

create.title: M1 r2-collapse obstruction and Hardy return map
create.statement_tex: M1 alone does not recombine to r_2(n)/4 times an n-only symbol: at X=y^2 and n=7, the active incidence (h,q)=(1,7) has nonzero weight while (7,1) lies beyond d<=y, so C_X^*(7) is nonzero although r_2(7)/4=chi_4(1)+chi_4(7)=0. If all divisor angles were instead completed to the full r_2(n)/4 coefficient through n asymp X^(1/2), the exact stationary constant reproduces the classical truncated Hardy--Voronoi radial sum; Popov Theorem 5 makes a target bound for that complete sum equivalent to the Gauss-circle target up to O_epsilon(X^(1/4+epsilon)). This obstruction does not rule out cancellation in the actual angular coefficient.
create.next_action: Retain the divisor-dependent angular symbol; do not replace it by r_2 or import the completed radial sum as an easier theorem.

reject.reason: The exact coefficient retains a divisor-angle symbol; at X=y^2,n=7 the (1,7) incidence is active and the cancelling (7,1) incidence is absent.
